$comment: 🔒 HUMAN-OWNED — CLAUDE.md §4.3. Spec versions and ruleset hashes.
⚠️ RESOLVE FROM PRIMARY SOURCE IN WEEK 1. Every `version` below is the
RESOLVE_IN_WEEK_1 sentinel, not a real specification version. The sentinel
is load-bearing: while it is present, apps/validator refuses to report a
conformance outcome for that profile unless CDL_ALLOW_PROVISIONAL_RULESET=1
is set (which only the corpus runner and the test suite do).
`ruleset_hash` is the sha256 of the compiled ruleset: every Schematron file
the profile declares, plus every code list, because code lists are inlined
into compiled tests and therefore change results. It is asserted against
the live registry by apps/validator/tests/test_specs_registry.py, so an
un-committed ruleset edit fails `make check` rather than drifting quietly.
The hashes below WILL change when the published Schematron replaces the
provisional one. That is the point — see apps/validator/src/validator/specs/RULES.md.
2026-07-29: the published rulesets have been OBTAINED and vendored under
apps/validator/src/validator/specs/*/published/ (provenance and upstream
commits: specs/PROVENANCE.md). They are NOT wired in — the engine cannot
execute them (specs/ENGINE-SVRL-MIGRATION.md). `published_source` below
records the version each profile WILL declare once its ruleset actually
runs. `version` stays on the sentinel until then, deliberately: it is the
gate that stops /validate reporting a verdict, and a real version string
beside a provisional ruleset would open that gate over a validator running
35 agent-authored rules. The version follows the ruleset, never leads it.
